source_fields.formulation: One learner must adapt simultaneously to all comparator paths without knowing their lengths. Losses are exponentially concave, and path length is Euclidean. Each round permits only a gradient at the chosen action.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: The compact convex set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$ is public and has Euclidean diameter at most $D$. Losses are $\eta$-exp-concave on $W$ and satisfy $\|\nabla f_t(w)\|_2\le G$; arbitrary admissible sequences are allowed. $$e^{-\eta f_t(\cdot)}\ \text{on }W\text{ is concave}.$$ Precisely, for each round $t$, the map $x\mapsto\exp(-\eta f_t(x))$ is concave on the feasible domain. This concerns the full action variable, with the stated norm and gradient bounds.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: $D$: $D\ge0$ (public); $G$: $G>0$ (public); $T$: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); $d$: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public); $\eta$: $\eta>0$ (public); $P$: $0\le P\le D(T-1)$ (hidden or used only in the analysis).

operations.query_signature: Submit the final action $w_t\in W$, then receive only $\nabla f_t(w_t)$. Full-function feedback and additional value or gradient evaluations at other points are unavailable. Exact Mahalanobis projection onto the public set is allowed, with arithmetic cost $C_{\mathrm{proj}}(d)$ per projection. The learner is causal and feasible. Inputs $d,T,D,G,\eta,W$ are public; comparator path budget $P_T^{(2)}$ is hidden. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

source_fields.complete_expression: One algorithm gives the pathwise exp-concave branch for comparator paths on its stated parameter window. The multibranch minimum under full-function feedback does not transfer to this interface. Here $c>0$ is the constant in the corresponding upper bound. For dimension dependence, $D,G,\eta$ is fixed independently of $d,T$.
aggregation_order: One algorithm gives the pathwise exponentially concave branch bound for comparator paths within its parameter window. The minimum frontier across branches under full-function feedback cannot be transferred directly to this interface.
Here $c>0$ is the constant used by the corresponding atomic upper bound. In dimension-dependent comparisons, $D,G,\eta$ is fixed and does not vary with $d,T$.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One admissible algorithm using only public information must handle every prescribed instance; adaptation to unknown budgets must be performed by that same algorithm.
randomness_sources: Observation or environment randomness explicitly allowed by the oracle.
source_fields.runtime_guarantee: The resource budget is fixed. Expected error is not automatically converted to high probability or a random-runtime bound.
